ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A transverse simple harmonic wave propagates along the positive $x$-axis with a wave speed of $v{=}6.0\mathrm{m/s}$. At time $t{=}0$, the waveform is as shown in the figure, and the displacement of particle $P$ is $10\mathrm{cm}$.

1. What is the vibration period of the particle $P$?
2. Starting from the moment $t{=}0$ (as shown in the figure), how long does it take for particle $P$ to reach the wave crest for the first time?
3. Indicate the direction of vibration of particle $P$ at the moment $t{=}1.1\mathrm{s}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph shows y in cm versus x in m at t=0. The wave amplitude is 20 cm, with a crest at x=0.6 m and y=20 cm, a trough at x=1.8 m and y=-20 cm, and one complete wavelength extending from x=0 to x=2.4 m. Point P is marked at x=1.0 m with displacement y=10 cm, on the descending part of the curve. Reasoning: From the graph, the wavelength is lambda=2.4 m. With wave speed v=6.0 m/s, the period is T=lambda/v=2.4/6.0=0.4 s. Since the wave propagates in the +x direction, the crest initially at x=0.6 m reaches the fixed particle at P, x=1.0 m, after traveling 1.0-0.6=0.4 m. Thus the first time for P to reach the crest is Delta t=0.4/6.0=1/15 s. For t=1.1 s, use the right-moving wave phase coordinate x_phase=x-vt=1.0-6.0(1.1)=-5.6 m. Adding three wavelengths gives -5.6+3(2.4)=1.6 m, which lies on the negative-slope part of the displayed waveform between x=1.2 m and x=1.8 m. For a right-moving wave, y_t=-v y_x, so a negative spatial slope means positive vertical velocity. Therefore P is vibrating along the +y direction at t=1.1 s.
